ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — James Madison Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for two years of recurrent sudden episodes of unresponsiveness, with low mood and anxiety, on levetiracetam started without a diagnosis. Concerns: For two years he has had sudden spells in which his mind seems to stop; he is afraid of having one in public or at the wheel; He feels low and worried, and does not expect to live long; He wants to know whether he has epilepsy and whether he can study law and take part in public life. [S]

tr.td: Levetiracetam 500 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice daily, started at an emergency department visit four months before intake for possible seizures, without an EEG
Levetiracetam 500 mg oral tablet, taper: half a tablet (250 mg) twice daily for two weeks, then half a tablet at night for one week, then stop
Half a tablet twice daily for two weeks, then half a tablet at night for one week, then stop
Sertraline 50 mg oral tablet, half a tablet (25 mg) each morning for one week, then one tablet (50 mg) each morning
Half a tablet each morning for one week, then one tablet each morning
Ondansetron 4 mg orally disintegrating tablet, one tablet every 8 hours as needed for vomiting, for up to three days
One tablet every 8 hours as needed for vomiting, up to three days

value.displayName: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate

tr.td: Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 76 per minute; normal PR, QRS, and QTc (404 ms); no pre-excitation, Brugada pattern, or heart block
MRI of the brain with an epilepsy protocol (3 tesla, thin coronal sections through the hippocampi): normal; no hippocampal sclerosis, cortical malformation, or other lesion

Inpatient video-EEG monitoring for 72 hours with sleep deprivation, hyperventilation, and photic stimulation, levetiracetam continued: two habitual events captured (2 minutes 40 seconds and 6 minutes), each with eyes closed and resisting opening, fluctuating unresponsiveness, and slow side-to-side head movements, during which the EEG showed a continuous normal waking posterior rhythm with no ictal or postictal change; normal interictal EEG awake and asleep; he confirmed both events as typical

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: A frail and sickly child, by the Library of Congress's account
Infirm health at college, which he put down to doing two years' work in one; for months he slept only three hours a night
Wrote that he felt dull and infirm and did not expect a long or healthy life

Generalized anxiety disorder: worry about his future, his health, and his studies most days for more than a year, with restlessness, poor sleep, and muscle tension (GAD-7 14 at intake): active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Primary care visit for two years of recurrent sudden episodes of unresponsiveness, with low mood and anxiety, on levetiracetam started without a diagnosis
Discharge-day review after video-EEG monitoring: diagnosis, its explanation, and the epilepsy and functional neurological disorder consultation
Six-week review after the diagnosis: levetiracetam withdrawn, psychotherapy under way, mood and anxiety
Three-month review after completing psychotherapy: events, mood, driving, and his studies
Same-day sick visit for viral gastroenteritis

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnostic workup: a detailed history including a witness account or phone video if available, ECG, blood count, metabolic panel, TSH, brain MRI with an epilepsy protocol, and inpatient video-EEG monitoring to capture his habitual events; levetiracetam continued unchanged until the evaluation is complete

Safety now: no driving until the evaluation is complete and the neurologist advises; showers rather than baths, no swimming alone or working at heights; seizure first aid for the people he lives and works near

Suicide risk assessment with a written safety plan: warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; the rifle locked with the ammunition stored separately; safety reviewed at every visit
Neurology consultation (epilepsy and functional neurological disorder) with admission for video-EEG monitoring, on the diagnosis, the antiseizure medicine, and treatment

Explaining the diagnosis: functional/dissociative seizures named and explained in person and in writing as real, common, and not epilepsy or feigning; how the brain can switch off awareness under strain; why antiseizure medicines do not help; that treatment works; a reliable written and online resource; a follow-up appointment to answer questions
Levetiracetam withdrawn: 250 mg twice daily for two weeks, 250 mg at night for one week, then stopped; no driving during the taper

CBT-informed psychotherapy for functional seizures: twelve weekly sessions with a psychologist experienced in functional neurological disorder, with an event diary, recognition of warning sensations, grounding techniques, work on avoidance, sleep, and worry, and a relapse-prevention plan

Measurement-based care for depression and anxiety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at least monthly during treatment; psychotherapy, an SSRI such as sertraline, or both, by shared decision once the cause of the events is clear

Studies and daily life: a regular sleep window of at least seven hours, study blocks with breaks, academic accommodations for testing (extra breaks), and a return to civic meetings with a friend who knows the first-aid plan
Driving: may resume once free of events for at least three months and with the neurologist's agreement, following state licensing rules and the AAN 2025 position
Cause of the episodes established by the second visit
Functional/dissociative seizures documented by video-EEG; epilepsy and syncope excluded
Levetiracetam tapered over three weeks and stopped, with no change in events and less irritability
Events reduced by at least half, then free of events for three months
From two or three a month to one in the last two months; none for five weeks
Depression and anxiety improved by at least 50 percent (PHQ-9 and GAD-7)

list.item: Independent in all activities; has stopped going to evening civic meetings for fear of an event in public; drove until intake, with no events at the wheel [S]

Slight, quiet, courteous, and precise in speech; mood "flat, and worried about everything"; affect constricted; thought process logical; no psychotic features; no suicidal ideation, intent, or plan; says he does not expect to live long but has no wish to die; insight good [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-04-07: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. No suicidal ideation, intent, plan, or behavior (C-SSRS screen negative; PHQ-9 item 9 scored 0); a fatalistic sense that he will not live long, without any wish to die. Moderate depression and anxiety with recurrent events raise risk, so: outpatient care with a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number, the rifle locked and the ammunition stored separately, and safety review at every visit [S]
